analysis:
The unit is the head-side tail (lines 651-1184) of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Startup/StartupPreloadTests.swift. It is a test-only file. The patch excerpt shows added test recorder events and a shapeWarmup dependency stub, and the 311-341 range was rewritten to park the load on an async gate with a 30s fail-safe race.

I found no production code changes, so none of these touch the trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007), attestation, the key handling assets (A-003, A-001) or the cache policy mitigations (T-041). The tests do not weaken any control.

One point I checked in the tests: makeFakeHFSnapshot (lines 858-870) writes into the real user HF cache via ModelScanner.defaultCacheDirectory(). It uses a UUID-suffixed id and the callers clean up with defer. This is a test-hygiene matter, not a security regression. It would only matter if the test ran against a developer's real cache, and the id namespace is unique.

The tests cover and assert security-relevant behaviors: fail-closed self-test retirement removes a model from the advertised set and forces a re-register without it, and the no-evict load path refuses instead of evicting. They also check that the startup self-test does not seed a tiny-prompt performance estimate, so this does not publish capacity-spoofable metrics. They assert these behaviors rather than changing them.

I could not see the production implementation of the shapeWarmup path or the earlier part of the file, because they are outside this unit and the patch excerpt is truncated. Nothing in the visible evidence indicates a security issue.
